first_impression.reaction: Searched 'greece wedding cost' and the intro tells me there's no number. My first thought was 'here we go, gated pricing'. But it says why, plainly, and doesn't pretend otherwise, so I jumped to the FAQ and the package and payment sections like I always do. It read more like a checklist than a sales page, which is why I stayed.

journey.quote: It depends on the wedding you plan. Island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel all move the total.
journey.reaction: This is the first answer I read and it's the non-answer I expected. 'It depends' is true, but it's also what every vendor says right before they ask for my email. The second sentence helps a bit, the first one is a shrug.

journey.quote: The total depends on the drivers above: island and venue, date, guest list, legal route, the events across the weekend and what you cover for guests. Ask each venue to quote against the same written brief, then compare line by line.
journey.reaction: No figure, so I'll get numbers elsewhere. But 'same written brief, compare line by line' is how I'd actually do it in a spreadsheet. Grudging respect.

journey.quote: Anything not written in the package is not included.
journey.reaction: Good. Blunt and correct. That's the kind of line that tells me they're not trying to hide the catch.

journey.quote: Taxes and service charges, and whether they sit inside the quoted price.
journey.reaction: This is exactly where I got burned last time. Seeing it called out means someone has thought about the gotchas.

journey.quote: An overseas business selling directly to Australian consumers must follow the Australian Consumer Law, but a remedy can be hard to obtain in practice; the consumer protection agency where the seller is based may help.
journey.reaction: Honest about the limitation instead of waving 'you're protected' at me. Linked to the ACCC, dated November 2026. This is the most credible bit of the page.

journey.section: Season and day of the week
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller says heatwaves are frequent in Greece over the summer months, and wildfires occur in the extended summer period from June to September.
journey.reaction: Sourced and dated. I can check it. That's what I want.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and has inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit. Begin with [Wedded Concierge]
journey.reaction: Right after the insurance and medical care paragraph, out of nowhere, a sales line. It's in the middle of the legal section, which makes it feel like the consumer-rights bit was a set-up for the pitch. Also, quoting in AUD is nice, but who carries the exchange-rate risk, and is there a margin on the conversion?

journey.quote: How is your fee set, and is it agreed in writing before work begins?
journey.reaction: Good question. So answer it for yourselves. You tell me to ask every planner this, then never say how your own fee is set. That's the one thing I came here to find out.

journey.quote: Which suppliers sit inside your quote, and which do we contract directly?
journey.reaction: Close to my real question but it dodges it. The question I'd ask is whether the planner takes a commission or mark-up from those suppliers. It's not on the list, which makes me wonder if that's deliberate.

journey.section: Planning your Greece wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Agreed in writing' is better than nothing, but it's not a fee model. Flat fee? Percentage of spend? Supplier commissions? Without that I can't put you in my comparison sheet next to the other two planners.

journey.section: Why there is no single Greece wedding cost
journey.quote: One couple marries at a town hall with a long lunch for close family. Another takes a clifftop venue for the weekend, hosts a welcome dinner and covers ferries for every guest.
journey.reaction: Fine as an illustration, but this is where a real wedding with the actual budget would win me over. Two hypothetical couples isn't proof.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor's fee calculated: flat fee, percentage of total spend, or something else?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from venues or suppliers it recommends, and is that shown on my quote?
When you quote in AUD, who carries the exchange-rate risk between quote and payment, and is there a margin built into the conversion?
Is there a real Greece wedding you've planned with the actual budget broken down?
What does an initial conversation with Wedded Concierge cost me, if anything, and what am I committing to by enquiring?
If a supplier you booked fails to deliver, who do I chase: you or the supplier?

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and has inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit. Begin with [Wedded Concierge]
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA dropped into the middle of the consumer-rights and insurance section, before the page has told me anything about how the planner is paid. Feels like the legal info was there to soften me up.

turn_offs_found.quote: It depends on the wedding you plan.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads as a dodge. It's the first thing I see in the FAQ, which is where I go first.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the 'Items quoted separately' list and the planner questions to use on the other two planners

cta_reaction.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: The checklist content is solid and honest, so the brand isn't ruled out. But I enquire only once my main questions are answered, and the big one, how you get paid and whether you take a cut from suppliers, isn't. I'd more likely use these questions on the other planners and come back if the fee model is published somewhere.

top_3_changes: Add the commission question to the planner list. old: "- Which suppliers sit inside your quote, and which do we contract directly?" new: "- Which suppliers sit inside your quote, and which do we contract directly?\n- Do you receive a commission or mark-up from any supplier you recommend, and will it be shown on our quote?"

Make the first FAQ answer less of a shrug. old: "It depends on the wedding you plan. Island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel all move the total." new: "There is no honest single figure, because island, venue, season, guest numbers and guest travel all move the total. A written quote against your own brief is the only number worth comparing."

Take the sales line out of the consumer-rights section so the legal information doesn't read as a lead-in to a pitch. old: "Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and has inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit. Begin with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-cost&utm_content=primary)." new: "" (the closing section already carries the CTA; if CRO needs a mid-article CTA, move the same sentence to the end of 'Written quotes' rather than after the insurance paragraph).
